messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] 100MB file limit for uploads
parts:
Hi Boris,
Unfortunately the change to support larger uploads wasn't quite as simple as I was hoping it would be.  I spent a little time with this and tested out a download from dropbox for a file that is publicly viewable.  Here is what I did using a package called downloader:

Within global.R  (or before your shinyServer function ) you would have logic that looks something like this:

library(downloader)

URL <- "https://......"
download(URL, destfile = "./filename")

If you wanted to make it a little smarter, you could check to see if the file is there and not bother downloading it if it has already been downloaded. (file.exists , and file.info would be what I would look at)

We will come up with a more elegant solution for folks.  Please let me know if this works for you.
-
Tareef

Le vendredi 20 mars 2015 18:07:55 UTC+1, Tareef Kawaf a écrit :
Hi Boris,
Unfortunately the change to support larger uploads wasn't quite as simple as I was hoping it would be.  I spent a little time with this and tested out a download from dropbox for a file that is publicly viewable.  Here is what I did using a package called downloader:

Within global.R  (or before your shinyServer function ) you would have logic that looks something like this:

library(downloader)

URL <- "https://......"
download(URL, destfile = "./filename")

If you wanted to make it a little smarter, you could check to see if the file is there and not bother downloading it if it has already been downloaded. (file.exists , and file.info would be what I would look at)

We will come up with a more elegant solution for folks.  Please let me know if this works for you.
-
Tareef

parts:
Hi Tareef,

I encountered a similar issue and your approach worked -- thank you for the walk-trough. However, there was a problem others may encounter also:

The default Startup Timeout may be insufficient to download large datasets. Specifically, it was insufficient for ~250Mb download and start-up in my case. Even the 300-sec. maximum could be too low to download and load datasets near 1Gb, depending on the source.

In the end, it would be great to have a more direct path for deploying large datasets.

Thank you and good luck working on the more elegant solution,
Greg
